text: Delete(P) and Insert(G) could land on different VChannels and commit in separate WAL transactions, so a snapshot could keep the delete and lose the entity. Proxy now queries the PKs first: an existing key is kept (Delete(P) + Insert(P)), a key not found gets an allocator-generated ID, and a row with no key is rejected. The caller's key is only a lookup key; allocator ownership keeps it from colliding with future inserts (20260803-autoid-upsert-primary-key-preservation.md).
